title: Junta Airstrike Near U Raz Mountain Pagoda in Ponnagyun Kills Two, Damages Historic Site
detail: A junta fighter jet dropped bombs near the U Raz Mountain suspension bridge in Ponnagyun Town, Rakhine State, around 12:30 p.m. on September 13, 2026, with one bomb landing on the creek bank and another exploding in the water near passenger motorboats. U Moe Moe, a 65-year-old boat worker from Lay Kan village, and Daw Soe Soe, 37, from Seti Yin village, were killed instantly; three others were injured by shrapnel. A separate bomb struck the upper section of the historic U Yit Taw (Uri Taung) Pagoda, causing partial structural collapse. The strike came amid the SAC's continuing 'Operation 4926' offensive against the Arakan Army around Sittwe and Ponnagyun.

media.caption: Aftermath of the September 13 airstrike near U Raz Mountain (Uri Taung) Pagoda, Ponnagyun Town.

title: KIA-Led Forces Sink or Damage Six Junta Vessels Between Sawati and Mya Lel Villages
detail: KIA-led resistance forces ambushed a flotilla of Military Commission vessels travelling downstream from Bhamo toward Mandalay on the morning of September 13, 2026, between Sawati and Mya Lel villages in Kachin State. Four vessels sank and two were badly damaged by fire. The junta retaliated with at least 15 bombing runs by Y-12 aircraft and fighter jets against Sawati, Kaung Tong and Nyaung Pin Thar villages. Resistance sources say roughly 24 military and cargo vessels have been destroyed and 151 Military Commission personnel captured in the Bhamo river campaign since late August.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the September 13 KIA-led ambush on junta vessels near Sawati and Mya Lel villages.

title: KIA-Led Forces Ambush Junta Reinforcement Column Near Kaung Ja Yang, Killing 40+
detail: Fighting broke out near Kaung Ja Yang village, Bhamo Township, on September 12, 2026, and escalated on September 13 when KIA-led allied forces surrounded and ambushed a roughly 100-troop junta reinforcement column — reportedly consisting largely of newly conscripted soldiers — advancing from Infantry Battalion 47. More than 40 soldiers were killed; survivors retreated toward Si Hai carrying wounded and bodies. Clearance operations through the morning of September 14 recovered 40+ bodies and captured over 30 soldiers alive along with weapons and ammunition.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the Sept 12-14 Kaung Ja Yang ambush near Bhamo.

title: Lin Yone Nyi Naung Guerrilla Force Ambushes Convoy Between Monywa and Sagaing, Killing 20+ Soldiers
detail: The Linn Yone Nyi Naung Guerrilla Force said it mined a military convoy travelling from the Northwestern Regional Military Command in Monywa toward the 33rd Light Infantry Division on September 13, 2026, then fired an 80mm weapon at troops caught in the resulting ambush. The group claimed more than 20 military personnel were killed. A civilian man working in a nearby peanut field was killed and another wounded when the military returned fire.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the September 13 Monywa-Sagaing convoy ambush.

title: Junta Powered Paraglider Kills 6, Including 4 Women and 2 Children, in Minhla Township
detail: A Myanmar military powered paraglider bombed Zun Kya village, Minhla Township, Magway Region, on September 13, 2026, killing six people — including four women and two children aged 70 and 15.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the September 13 paraglider bombing of Zun Kya village.

title: ~80 Junta POWs Escape PDF-Zoland Detention Facility in Tedim Township
detail: Roughly 80 prisoners of war held by PDF-Zoland — including majors and captains captured in fighting linked to the Kennedy Peak battle — overpowered guards, seized firearms and unlocked cells to escape a detention facility in Tedim Township, Chin State, on the night of September 13, 2026.
